case_001.title: The Storage Room Murder
beats: Marcus found the ledger page proving I had taken money from the cafe till for my mother's care.
He gave me until morning to confess, then summoned me to the storage room before opening.
I lied about the fountain, doubled back through the alley, and entered by the rear door.
Marcus refused to back down. I took the brass till weight and struck him once.
That was the thud Ben and Priya heard at seven fifty-six. Marcus fell where I hit him.
I rinsed the weight in the kitchen, then hid it at the bottom of the mop bucket.
I opened the cafe two minutes late and kept repeating a fountain alibi nobody could confirm.
I killed Marcus to hide what I stole, but every physical trace led back to me.

case_002.title: The Locked Bookshop
beats: I forged Isabella's signature on the partnership transfer because I did not trust her to agree.
The solicitor's letter said she had discovered it and would expose me that afternoon.
Ben saw us arguing in the bookshop back room, beside Isabella's desk and telephone.
When she reached for the telephone, I seized the brass letter opener and struck her.
I smashed the window from inside to make the killing look like an interrupted burglary.
The glass fell the wrong way. My green scarf also snagged on the rear-door latch.
I fled through the alley and invented a stockroom alibi, but the invoice timestamp disproved it.
I killed Isabella to preserve a partnership that had never truly belonged to me.

case_003.title: The Clinic After Hours
beats: Elias planned to remove the clinic from his will, destroying everything I had built around his bequest.
At four thirty, I added two digoxin capsules to his Tuesday pill compartment.
It was four times his safe dose. I altered the dispensary log to conceal the missing capsules.
At five past five, I delivered the organiser myself, as I always did.
Ruth saw the handoff. I watched Elias take the pills and left him on the clinic bench.
His heart condition made the overdose look natural. He was dead by five twenty-one.
The spilled flask, open organiser, altered log, and my private budgets exposed the plan.
I poisoned Elias because I valued the clinic he promised me more than his life.

case_004.title: The Fountain at Midnight
beats: I found twelve years of letters proving Owen had blackmailed my father over the village hall fire.
I cancelled my plans with Priya and crossed the square to confront him at the fountain.
Owen laughed. He said my father had come to him, as though the extortion meant nothing.
I seized a loose stone from the fountain coping and struck Owen with it.
Nadia heard our voices. Elias saw me leave quickly after the blow at the fountain.
Priya tried to protect me with an alibi, but my cancellation message proved she lied.
Mud on my jacket and a matching bootprint placed me beside the fountain that night.
I killed Owen in anger for what he did to my father, then let Priya lie for me.

case_005.title: The Rear Alley Fire
beats: I called Clara at six twenty and told her to meet me in the rear alley at seven.
I chose it because Elias could not see the alley. I came through the back lane.
Clara knew I forged the mortgage on Hobbs Cafe. The estate wanted eight thousand pounds.
I panicked. I pulled my builder's belt around her throat until she stopped fighting.
I burned the letter and lit the wet crates, hoping the fire would hide what I had done.
The fire went out. I returned up the lane holding my trousers and made Col lie.
Page two remained on the cafe counter. It gave me twelve months to put everything right.
I never read it. I killed Clara for a letter that was trying to save me.

case_006.title: The Bell Estate
beats: Marcus was my half-brother, though the Bell family refused to acknowledge me for twenty years.
His new will meant I would have to expose our parentage publicly and fight for everything.
I harvested foxglove from my garden and extracted the digitalis hidden inside it.
Using my spare key, I entered Marcus's house at nine while he was away.
I poured the poison into his prepared cocoa and burned a copy of my birth certificate.
Marcus drank it later. His heart failed at ten forty, appearing to be natural causes.
The cracked vial, cut foxgloves, mug residue, and hidden birth certificate exposed me.
I poisoned my own brother before his will could erase me from the Bell family again.

case_007.title: The Man Who Saw Everything
beats: Thirty years ago, I forged Thomas Hobbs's signature and used the bill of sale to take his cafe.
Elias found his old notebook recording me practising that signature against the schoolhouse glass.
He ordered me to give the cafe to the village trust before the nine o'clock reading.
I left the fair on a false cup errand and went through my kitchen to the dark alley.
Elias left the stockroom door open. When he refused my offer, I struck him from behind.
I used the cast-iron owl doorstop, wiped it, then hid his notebook beneath my coat.
I returned before nine, breathless and empty-handed, and hid the notebook with the spare cups.
I killed the only man who knew what my life stood on, but the village reconstructed every minute.
